chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Sulaymān al-Dahhān, from Rifāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“ʿUmar was approached by a man from Qays with a mawlā of his who had struck his eye, causing fluid to descend into it while it remained standing, yet he could not see anything with it. So he said to him: ‘I will give you the diyah,’ but he refused.”

He said: “So he sent them both to ʿAlī عليه السلام and said: ‘Judge between these two.’ So he offered him the diyah, but he refused.” He said: “They continued offering him more until they offered him two diyahs.” He said: “Then he said: ‘I want nothing but qiṣāṣ.’”

He said: “Then ʿAlī عليه السلام called for a mirror and heated it. Then he called for cotton and moistened it. Then he placed it upon the edges of his eyes and around them. Then he faced the sun directly with his eyes.”
He said: “And he brought the mirror and said: ‘Look.’ So he looked, and the fatty substance melted while his eye remained standing, and the sight went away.”

key_terms.عَيْنَهُ: his eye, the injured organ in the case
key_terms.مَوْلًى: a dependent or client associated with a man
key_terms.مِرْآةٍ: a mirror used in carrying out the judicial procedure
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةَ: financial compensation paid for bodily injury
key_terms.ٱلْقِصَاصَ: retaliatory legal retribution corresponding to the injury
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءَ: fluid that descended into the eye after the blow

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام judge a case of qiṣāṣ for an eye injury when the victim refused diyah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a case of injury to the eye in which compensation was refused and the injured party insisted on qiṣāṣ. Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام judged the matter and demonstrated a method by which the loss of sight could be inflicted while the eye itself remained intact, corresponding to the original injury. The report reflects judicial authority and legal precision in matters of retaliation and bodily injury.
